subject: DeltaAI dedicated capacity ask — shoulder contingency + preemptible fallback
messages:
From: Evelyn Ward <evelyn.ward@deltaai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity plan and preemptible fallback for DeltaAI (intent to commit)

Marcus / team,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciated the walkthrough. DeltaAI is preparing to move a large portion of our inference workload to dedicated capacity for predictable latency and data isolation. A quick summary of what we need help sizing and formalizing: 

- Steady-state inference footprint: ~60 A100-equivalent GPUs (24/7).
- Seasonal / product launches: short bursts up to +40 GPUs for 1–3 hour windows (several times a week) and occasional longer training runs that could need an extra 20–30 GPUs for a few days.
- Objective: a reserved baseline for steady traffic plus a shoulder/burst strategy that keeps our 99th latency SLO intact while minimizing monthly committed spend.

We are open to using preemptible (spot) capacity as a low-cost burst option, but need clear eviction behavior, throttling policy, and an SLA/credit model if preemptible eviction materially impacts our synchronous inference latency. Attached is our capacity_request spreadsheet with hourly profiles for the next 12 months.

Questions for you:
1) Can you propose a recommended reserved slab + shoulder pool + preemptible fallback that balances cost and latency?
2) What autoscale and eviction controls do you recommend (grace periods, notify-before-evict, gentle-throttle vs immediate reject)?
3) If we commit to a 12-month reserved slab, what pricing/discounts do you typically offer when combined with a preemptible burst pool?

Would like a one-hour design + commercial deep-dive tomorrow (UTC-8 late morning) if possible.

Thanks,
Evelyn Ward
Head of Platform
DeltaAI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity plan and preemptible fallback for DeltaAI (intent to commit)

Evelyn — thanks for the detailed profile and for the call. Replying with a high-level engineering proposal before we dive tomorrow so we have something concrete to iterate on.

Summary proposal (high-level):
- Reserved slab: 80 vGPUs (covers steady-state 60 + buffer for KPIs and warm-up).
- Shoulder pool (hot standby): 40 vGPUs in a warm pool (prefetched KV caches, preloaded models). This pool sits in the same tenancy and can be promoted within ~30–90s for warm calls.
- Preemptible fallback: 50 preemptible vGPUs across adjacent AZs for stochastic bursts. Eviction model: 2-minute eviction notice via API/webhook; graceful throttle for synchronous requests (return 503+retry-after) with automatic routing to smaller model variant if latency SLO would break.

Autoscale policy suggestions:
- Scale triggers: rolling window 60s 95th-percentile latency breach OR 5-minute sustained token rate above reserved capacity threshold.
- Cool-down: 3 minutes for scale-up, 15 minutes for scale-down to prevent oscillation.
- Priority queueing: reserved slab requests > shoulder > preemptible. Preemptible used only after shoulder depleted or explicitly allowed for non-critical inference.
- Warm-up: KV cache population jobs triggered when shoulder pool is created; model quantization tier fallback available for extreme pressure.

Risks & mitigations:
- Preemptible eviction can spike latency. Mitigation: route to reduced-capacity model (quantized) or return early with model-level degrade. Also we can set a soft-threshold where we proactively spin the shoulder pool when forecasted traffic > 75% of reserved slab.
- Cross-region routing adds 10–30ms RTT; prefer in-region headroom first.

I'll attach a one-page PDF with a diagram and the param table (DeltaAI_capacity_plan_v1.pdf). For the deep-dive tomorrow, we'd like to run a short simulation against the hourly profile you sent so we can size the warm-up lead time and compute expected preemptible consumption.

Proposed times: 11:00–12:00 PST (tomorrow) or 14:00–15:00 PST. Let me know which works.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DeltaAI dedicated capacity ask — commercial sketch + next steps

Evelyn — looping in commercial details per Marcus's proposal. Short sketch of terms to inform your procurement team: 

- Baseline reserved commit: 80 vGPUs (12-month term). List price equivalent: $135,000 / month.
- Shoulder pool: configuration option; charged as standby capacity at $0.60 per vGPU-hour when actively promoted, free while warm (limited to X hours/month) — we can model different approaches.
- Preemptible burst consumption: $2.75 per vGPU-hour consumed (billed only for used hours).
- SLA: 99.5% uptime for reserved slab with SLA credits. Preemptible pool explicitly excluded from latency SLA; we provide a preemptible addendum that guarantees a notify-before-evict webhook and a 30-minute mitigation window for high-severity incidents.
- Discounting: with a 12-month commit and 12-month billing prepay we can offer a 12–18% effective discount depending on volume mix.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Sign a narrow amendment for reserved slab + preemptible addendum (DocuSign link below).
2) Run two capacity simulations (Marcus's team) on your hourly profile to validate warm-up lead times and preemptible exposure.
3) Schedule a 60–90 minute technical + procurement review (we can include finance) — proposed slot tomorrow 11:00 PST.

DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/Contract/DELTA-4921
Term sheet attached: DeltaAI_term_sheet_v1.xlsx

Happy to adjust numbers; wanted to get something on paper so your procurement can model TCO.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus / Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Procurement will review the term sheet this afternoon.

Can you include in tomorrow's deep-dive: a short capacity-runway simulation (hourly) that shows expected preemptible consumption under our profile, and a worst-case latency impact chart with and without the shoulder pool? Also please invite whoever manages the autoscale rules so we can confirm cooldown windows and webhook formats.

We can do 11:00–12:00 PST tomorrow. Please send an invite and the simulation artifacts 30 minutes beforehand.

Best,
Evelyn
Head of Platform, DeltaAI
